methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $356M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Gatik, a Series C autonomous freight company, operates in a Transportation sector with a sparse public comp universe (0 public peers) and 8 private frontier-tech peers including Rivian, The Boring Company, and Einride. The absence of same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with sufficient scale precludes reliance on peer-median multiples.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation tool. Using Gatik's $356M in total raised as a proxy for current enterprise value, the analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C to subsequent-stage advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $605M. This reflects anticipated value creation between current and next funding event absent transaction data or operational benchmarks.

The triangulated valuation range spans $514M (low) to $695M (high), with a median of $605M derived exclusively from stage-progression. Key uncertainties include the absence of margin-adjusted EBITDA comparables, limited visibility into unit economics, and the immature public market for autonomous freight operators. The single-method foundation makes this analysis sensitive to assumptions around typical step-up multiples and the representativeness of the $356M raised figure as a valuation proxy. Narrowing this range would require either emergence of late-stage private comps, near-term path to profitability, or public comparables in adjacent autonomous-vehicle segments.
